subject: zoology
question_text: How do you differentiate between growth in a living organism and growth in a non-living object?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.50, VSAQ 70). page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Growth in a living organism
steps.why: Growth in a living body comes from cell division inside it, so new material is added within and not on the surface — that is the one difference the whole answer rests on.
common_mistakes: Writing that living things grow by adding matter on the outside. That is how non-living objects grow.
Writing that growth in animals continues for life. Animal growth stops at a certain age.
steps.memory_tip: Living growth is from inside by cell division; non-living growth is from outside by added matter.
steps.margin_note: Definition first, then the living half. Three or four short lines.
lines: Growth is an increase in size and mass.
In a living organism growth takes place from
inside the body, by an increase in the number
of cells and in the size of the cells.
It is therefore called growth from inside, or
In animals growth stops at a certain age; in
plants it goes on through life.

steps.label: Growth in a non-living object
steps.why: A non-living object gains material only where the outside world touches it, so its growth is a surface process and stops the moment nothing more is added.
common_mistakes: Calling this true growth. It is only the piling up of matter, so it is not a sign of life.
steps.memory_tip: A sand mound grows only where sand lands on it: outside only.
steps.margin_note: The contrast in the same words as the living half, plus one example.

lines.text: Living grows from inside, non-living outside

lines: In a non-living object growth takes place by
the piling up (accretion) of matter on the
It is therefore called growth from outside, or
Example: a mound of sand grows taller as more
Such growth is not counted as a sign of life.

insider_note: The mark is for the contrast, not for the definition — write 'from inside by cell division' against 'from outside by piling up of matter', and give one non-living example.
